source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: Furthermore [or: again], it came to pass in those days that likewise a decree [went out] from Caesar Augustus that all the inhabited world should be registered [or: assessed, taxed]

translation_notes: עוד (consonants עוד): Candidates: H5749 'to testify, repeat', H5750 'again, furthermore', H5751 (same as H5750). Chose H5750 because it functions adverbially here introducing a new narrative event — 'again' or 'furthermore' fits the opening of a passage.
היה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist, be, become, come to pass', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 because the context requires a copulative/narrative verb 'it came to pass'.

שכל (consonants שכל): This is parsed as the relative particle ש + כל (H3605 'all, the whole'). The context 'that all the world' demands this compound reading rather than H7919 'to be intelligent' or H7921 'to miscarry'.
כן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so, thus', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because paired with כמו it forms the idiom 'like so / likewise'.
textual_notes: נוגש has no Strong's candidates listed but shares consonants with נגש (H5065 'to drive, exact, oppress, tax'). The context of a census/registration decree suggests 'taxed' or 'registered' — the word carries overtones of exacting or pressing for tribute.
ציווי appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew nominal form from צוה (H6680 'to command'); no exact Strong's match. It means 'a command, decree'.
מקיסר and גושט are transliterations of the Latin 'Caesar Augustus' — no Strong's entries exist for these foreign proper nouns.

verses.literal: Again [it] was done in those days like so a command from Caesar Augustus that all the world would be taxed

verses.translation: And this registration was first carried out while [the] lord [was] king [of Syria]. [The] way of peace to his people, [the] lovingkindness of ... the fathers on high, [for] us who are sitting [at] his feet ...

translation_notes: האדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign, controller', H114 'Addon (proper noun)'. Chose H113 because the text describes a ruling authority — 'the lord/governor king of Syria'.
מלך (consonants מלך): Candidates: H4427 'to reign', H4428 'a king', H4430 'a king (Aramaic)', H4432 'Molek'. Chose H4428 because the word is positioned as a noun title following 'the lord'.
במרום (consonants מרום): Candidates: H4791 'altitude, height', H4792 'Merom (a lake)'. Chose H4791 because 'the fathers on high/in the height' fits a liturgical or theological context.

חסד (consonants חסד): Candidates: H2616 'to be kind', H2617 'kindness, lovingkindness', H2618 'Chesed (proper noun)'. Chose H2617 because the noun 'kindness' fits the surrounding phrase about peace and blessing.
textual_notes: This section appears severely corrupted or is a composite of the narrative text with liturgical fragments. The sequence תהיו יהיו תהיו ת תהיינה appears to be scribal repetition or practice marks — multiple verb forms ('you will be', 'they will be', 'they (f.) will be') with no clear syntactic function.
אנור״ל appears to be an abbreviation (marked with ״) whose expansion is unknown. It may be a scribal gloss or reference mark.
דרךשלום appears written as one word, likely 'way of peace' (דרך + שלום). This phrase, along with what follows, may be a liturgical insertion or marginal note that was incorporated into the text.
הנגישה is a nominal/participial form derived from נגש — 'the taxing/registration', corresponding to the נוגש in section 1.

The phrase בעד האדון מלך של שיריאה is ambiguous: it could mean 'while [the] lord [was] king of Syria' (temporal) or 'on behalf of the lord king of Syria' (agential). The context of a first census under a specific governor suggests a temporal reading.

verses.literal: And this the taxing was done first for the lord king [of Syria] way-of-peace to-his-people kindness ... the fathers in the height us that we [are] sitting his feet ...

verses.translation: And all of them were going, each one to his [own] city, in order that they would obey [or: heed] his command — [the command] of the lord [or: sovereign]
words: in order that, on account of

translation_notes: אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify, collect thoughts', H259 'one, united, first'. Chose H259 because כל אחד is 'each one' — a standard distributive expression.

לעירו (consonants עירו): The listed candidate H5900 is 'Iru' (proper noun). However, the ל prefix + עיר + ו suffix clearly gives 'to his city' (from עיר H5892). The proper noun reading makes no contextual sense.
בעבור (consonants עבור): Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 because a purpose clause fits — they were going in order to comply.
של (consonants של): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of, which'. Chose H7945 because it serves as a genitive particle 'of' connecting 'his command' to 'the lord'.
האדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 — referring to the ruling authority who issued the decree.
textual_notes: שישמעו could mean 'that they would hear' or 'that they would obey' — שמע carries both senses. In context of a decree, 'obey/comply with' is the likely force.
האדון could refer to the earthly sovereign (Caesar/governor) or could carry a theological double meaning. The immediate narrative context points to the earthly ruler.

verses.literal: And all of them were going each one to his city in order that they would hear his command of the lord

verses.translation: And Joseph ascended from Nazareth of Galilee [going] into Judah, to the city of David which is called Bethlehem [House of Bread], because he was from the household and from the lineage [or: people] of David

translation_notes: עלה (consonants עלה): Candidates: H5927 'to ascend', H5928 'a holocaust', H5929 'a leaf', H5930 'stairs/holocaust', H5931 'a pretext'. Chose H5927 because the verb 'to go up' fits traveling from Galilee (lower elevation) to Judah (higher elevation).

בעיר (consonants בעיר/עיר): Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'a city', H5893 'Ir (proper noun)', H5894 'a watcher', H5895 'a young donkey'. Chose H5892 because 'to the city of David' is the clear sense in a travel narrative.
דוד (consonants דוד): Candidates: H1730 'beloved, uncle', H1731 'a pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 — the proper name David, as this refers to the ancestral city and lineage.

בית + לחם: בית — H1004 'house'; לחם — Candidates: H3898 'to consume/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread', H3901 'battle'. Together they form the place name Bethlehem ('House of Bread'). H3899 chosen for לחם.
ומעם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people, tribe', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 because 'from the people/lineage of David' parallels 'from the house of David'.
textual_notes: מנצרת has no Strong's listing — it is a transliteration of the place name Nazareth with the preposition מן (from).

בעבור שיהיה could mean 'in order that he would be [registered there]' (purpose) or 'because he was' (causal). Both are grammatically possible; the causal reading ('because he was from the house of David') explains why he specifically went to Bethlehem.

verses.literal: And Joseph went up from Nazareth [of] Galilee to Judah to [the] city [of] David that is called House of Bread in order that he would be from the house and from [the] people [of] David

verses.translation: In order to comply with [or: obey] the command, [together] with Miriam his betrothed — his wife — and she [was] pregnant [or: with child]

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5973 because 'with Miriam' indicates accompaniment — Joseph went to obey the decree together with Miriam.
הרה (consonants הרה): Candidates: H2029 'to become pregnant, conceive', H2030 'pregnant'. Chose H2030 because the adjective 'pregnant' describes Miriam's state at the time.
המצוה (consonants מצוה): Candidate H4687 'a command' fits perfectly; H6680 'to command' is the verbal root. The ה prefix makes this 'the command', pointing to the decree of section 1.
textual_notes: ארוסתו is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'his betrothed' (from ארוס), with no classical Strong's entry. It clearly denotes a woman pledged in marriage.

The juxtaposition of ארוסתו ואשתו ('his betrothed and his wife') is notable — it may indicate that the text preserves two traditions about her status, or that she was both betrothed and considered his wife.

verses.literal: In order that he would hear the command with Miriam his betrothed and his wife and she [was] pregnant

verses.translation: And while they were there, [the] days of Miriam were completed [or: fulfilled] to give birth

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who, which, when, where', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כ + אשר forms the conjunction 'when/as', introducing a temporal clause.
שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'a name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'a name'. Chose H8033 because the context indicates location — 'while they were there [in Bethlehem]'.

מלאו: Root מלא (H4390 'to fill, be full, complete'). No Strong's candidate was listed but this is clearly the 3rd person plural completed form 'were filled/completed'. The days of her pregnancy reached their fullness.
ללדת: ל (infinitive prefix) + ילד (H3205 'to bear, give birth') + ת (infinitive construct ending). 'To give birth.'

verses.literal: And when they were there days of Miriam were filled to give birth

verses.translation: And she gave birth there [to] her firstborn son, and they wrapped him in cloths [or: garments] and laid him in a feeding trough [or: manger] of the animals, because there was no other place [where she] could lay him — in that ledge [or: shelf] projecting from the wall outward, which they call 'porshi'

translation_notes: שם (consonants שם): Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Chose H8033 — 'she gave birth there' indicates location.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'because, for, that'. Chose H3588 — introduces the causal clause explaining why the manger was used.
לא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
מקום (consonants מקום): Candidates: H4725 'a place, standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 — 'there was no place' requires the noun.
אחר (consonants אחר): Candidates: H309 'to delay', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other, another', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 because 'another place' fits — no other place was available.
מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from, out of', H4481 'from (Aramaic)', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 — 'from the wall' describes the projection.
הקיר (consonants קיר): Candidates: H7023 'a wall', H7024 'Kir (a place)'. Chose H7023 — the physical wall from which the ledge projects.

הבהמות (consonants בהמות): H930 is listed as 'behemoth/hippopotamus', but the consonants are identical to the common plural of בהמה (H929 'beast, animal, cattle'). In context of a manger, domestic animals are meant.
textual_notes: וילדה is parsed as ו + ילדה (she gave birth), not as H3207 'a lass'. The vav-consecutive plus 3fs verb fits the narrative flow.
בנו: The suffix ו could be 'his' or 'her' depending on vocalization. Context (she gave birth to her son) suggests 'her son' though the consonants alone are ambiguous.

קרוי appears to be a passive participle ('that which is called/named') but in this context seems to refer to a physical structure — possibly a protruding shelf or niche in the wall. The word may function both as 'called' and as a noun for the structure itself.

פורשי is a foreign loanword or technical term — possibly from Old French 'porche' or similar Romance language term for a projecting structure/porch. No Hebrew Strong's entry exists. This suggests the manuscript was produced in a Romance-language environment.

The extended explanation about the wall-shelf called 'porshi' appears to be a scribal gloss explaining what kind of structure the manger was in — unusual for a narrative text and suggests a translator adding cultural context.

verses.literal: And she gave birth there [to] her son firstborn born and they wrapped him in garments and laid him in a manger of the beasts because not there was [a] place other [she] could lay him in that shelf going out from the wall to outside that they call porshi

verses.translation: And shepherds in that region [or: generation] were [out as] young men, keeping [the] watches of the night over their flocks [or: livestock]

translation_notes: הדור (consonants דור): Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate, remain', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'a circle/ball', H1755 'a generation, age; also a dwelling', H1756 'Dor (a place)'. Chose H1755. This could mean 'generation' (time period) or 'region/dwelling'. In context, 'in that region' makes good geographic sense (the area around Bethlehem), though 'generation' (era) is also possible.

על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top, aloft', H5921 'over, upon, against', H5922 (Aramaic same), H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'over their livestock' indicates the shepherds' responsibility.

שעות: No Strong's candidates directly listed. The consonants match שעה (H8160 Aramaic 'an hour' or post-biblical Hebrew 'hours'). The listed candidates עות (H5790 'to hasten', H5791 'to wrest') would require reading ש as a prefix, giving 'that they twisted/hastened', which makes no sense here. 'Hours/watches' fits — the watches of the night.
textual_notes: הדור could be 'the generation' (temporal — in that era) or could relate to 'dwelling/region' (H1755 secondary meaning). The narrative context allows either, but since באותו הדור parallels באותן הימים in section 1, the temporal reading 'in that period/generation' seems primary.
שעות as 'hours/watches' reflects post-biblical Hebrew usage. Classical Hebrew would use אשמרות for 'night watches'. This further suggests a medieval Hebrew composition or translation.

verses.literal: And shepherds in that generation were lads and keeping watches of the night over their livestock

verses.translation: And behold, an angel [or: messenger] of YHWH stood [or: was stationed] near to them, and the radiance [or: light] of YHWH was encircling [them] all around, and there came upon them a great dread [or: fear]

translation_notes: והנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo! behold!'. Chose H2009 — the interjection 'behold!' introduces a sudden dramatic event.
מלאך (consonants מלאך): Candidates: H4397 'a messenger, angel', H4398 'an angel (Aramaic)'. Chose H4397 — the Hebrew form for a divine messenger.
נצב (consonants נצב): Candidates: H5324 'to station, stand', H5325 'a handle'. Chose H5324 — the angel 'stood/was stationed' near them.

להם: The listed candidate H3859 'to burn in, rankle' requires reading להם as a verb, which makes no sense here. Reading as ל + הם (H1992 'them') gives 'to them', which is the obvious prepositional phrase.
ואור (consonants אור): Candidates: H215 'to make luminous', H216 'illumination, light', H217 'flame', H218 'Ur (a place)'. Chose H216 — 'the light/radiance of YHWH' as a noun subject.
והיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to be, come to pass', H1962 'ruin'. Chose H1961 — 'and there was to them' (i.e., they had/experienced).
פחד (consonants פחד): Candidates: H6342 'to fear', H6343 'dread, alarm', H6344 'a testicle'. Chose H6343 — the noun 'dread/fear' pairs with the adjective 'great'.

verses.literal: And behold a messenger of YHWH stationed near to them and light of YHWH surrounding around and there was to them dread great

verses.translation: And the angel [or: messenger] said to them: Do not fear! Behold, I [am] declaring [or: announcing] to you a great joy [or: gladness] that will be for all the people

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — the standard Hebrew verb 'said' in narrative.
אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God, mighty', H413 'to, near'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect verb (תפחדו) forms a negative command 'do not fear'.
הנה (consonants הנה): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'behold!'. Chose H2009 — introducing the announcement with dramatic emphasis.

מגיד: This is a hifil participle from נגד (H5046 'to declare, announce, tell'). The listed candidate H1517 'a tendon/sinew' (גיד) shares consonants but makes no sense. The מ prefix + גיד consonants as a hifil participle of נגד is the clear reading: 'one who declares/is declaring'.
שמחה (consonants שמחה): Candidates: H8057 'joy, gladness', H4229 'to wipe, erase'. Chose H8057 — 'great joy' is the natural reading after an angelic announcement.
העם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with'. Chose H5971 — 'all the people' as the recipients of the joyful news.
textual_notes: תפחדו has no separate Strong's listing but is clearly the 2nd person masculine plural imperfect of פחד (H6342 'to fear') — 'you shall fear / you will fear', here negated as a command: 'do not fear'.

verses.literal: And the messenger said to them do not fear behold I [am] declaring to you joy great that will be to all the people

verses.translation: For today [there] has been born to us in the city of David a deliverer [savior, rescuer] of the world [or: the age, eternity], who is [the] anointed one [Messiah] and sovereign [lord, master]
words: has been born (niphal perfect of ילד)

translation_notes: בעיר (consonants ב+עיר): Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (name)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass'. Chose H5892 because 'in the city of David' is a coherent place reference that fits a birth announcement, whereas 'in the cattle of David' or 'in the donkey of David' produces no real-world image.

דוד (consonants דוד): Candidates: H1730 'beloved/uncle', H1731 'pot/basket', H1732 'David'. Chose H1732 because paired with 'city of' it identifies a specific place (the city of David), producing a coherent geographical reference.

משיח (consonants משיח): Candidates: H4899 'anointed one/Messiah', H7878 'to ponder/converse', H7879 'contemplation', H7880 'a shoot/shrubbery'. Chose H4899 because the mem-prefix + שיח as 'anointed' fits the parallel with 'lord/sovereign' and the birth announcement context.
ואדון (consonants ו+אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (a name)'. Chose H113 because paired with 'anointed one' it forms a natural title pair in a birth proclamation.
textual_notes: העולם could mean 'the world' (spatial sense) or 'the age/eternity' (temporal sense). Both readings of H5769 are plausible. The spatial reading ('deliverer of the world') fits the grandeur of the announcement; the temporal reading ('deliverer of the age') is also coherent.

verses.literal: For the-day has-been-born to-us in-city-of David a-deliverer of-the-world who-[is] he anointed-one and-lord

verses.translation: And this will be the sign [signal, evidence] for you: you will find the child [boy, infant] wrapped [swaddled] in a garment [cloth, clothing] and placed [laid down] in a feeding-trough [manger]
words: and it will be (qal imperfect 3ms of היה with waw)
you will find (qal imperfect 2mp of מצא)
and laid / placed (hophal participle of נוח)

translation_notes: האות (consonants ה+אות): Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/evidence'. Chose H226 because 'this is the sign' introduces identifying evidence for locating the child, which is the contextual function here.

הנער (consonants ה+נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/child', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the context describes finding a specific infant who has been born.

בבגד (consonants ב+בגד): Candidates: H898 'to cover/act covertly', H899 'a covering/clothing'. Chose H899 because 'wrapped in a garment' produces a coherent image of a swaddled infant, and the preposition ב + noun is the natural parsing.
textual_notes: באיבוס has no Strong's candidates provided. The consonants א-י-ב-ו-ס correspond to a feeding-trough or manger (a loanword or late Hebrew term). No alternative reading is available from the provided data.
מעוטף could be parsed as a pual participle of עטף (to wrap/cover) or potentially from a related root. The wrapping/swaddling reading is most natural for a newborn child.

verses.literal: And-it-will-be to-you this the-sign you-will-find the-boy wrapped in-a-garment and-laid in-a-manger

verses.translation: And immediately [at once] there appeared with the messenger [angel] a great multitude of the heavenly host [army, force], giving praise [thanks, acknowledgment] to YHWH and saying
words: was made / appeared (niphal perfect 3ms of עשה)
and giving thanks (hiphil participle mp of ידה)
and saying (qal participle mp of אמר)

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5973 because 'appeared with the angel' makes sense—the host appeared alongside the messenger. 'A people the angel' would be grammatically awkward.
המלאך (consonants ה+מלאך): Candidates: H4397 'messenger/angel', H4398 'angel (Aramaic)'. Chose H4397 as the Hebrew form, since this text uses Hebrew syntax throughout this section.

חיל (consonants חיל): Candidates: H2426 'army/intrenchment', H2427 'a throe', H2428 'force/army/strength', H2429 'army (Aramaic)'. Chose H2428 because 'multitude of heavenly host/army' is the coherent image—a heavenly military force appearing with the angel.

הודאה (consonants הודאה): The provided candidates under דאה (H1675 'to fly', H1676 'kite') do not fit. The consonants הודאה naturally parse as a noun from the root ידה (to give thanks/praise), meaning 'thanksgiving/praise.' The Strong's candidates listed relate only to the final three consonants דאה, but the full form הודאה is a standard Hebrew noun for 'thanksgiving.' I read it as such.
textual_notes: ומיד literally means 'and from hand' but functions idiomatically as 'immediately/at once.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew usage.

הודאה: The Strong's candidates provided (H1675, H1676 under דאה) do not match the word. The form הודאה is a well-known noun meaning 'thanksgiving/acknowledgment' from ידה. No Strong's number is provided for this reading.
שממיי has no Strong's candidates provided. It appears to be an adjective 'heavenly' derived from שמים (sky/heaven). The doubled מ and yod ending suggest an adjectival form.

verses.literal: And-immediately was-made with the-messenger a-multitude-of host heavenly and-giving-thanks thanksgiving to-YHWH and-saying

verses.translation: Exaltation [glory, highest praise] will be to God [the Mighty One] most high, and on the earth peace [wholeness, well-being, prosperity] to people of good favor [delight, goodwill]

translation_notes: לאל (consonants ל+אל): Candidates: H3815 'Lael (name)', H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'to God most high' forms a coherent phrase of divine praise. 'To Lael most high' or 'to not most high' make no sense.
עליון (consonants עליון): Candidates: H5945 'the Supreme/lofty', H5946 'the Supreme (Aramaic)'. Chose H5945 as the Hebrew form, modifying 'God.'

שלום (consonants שלום): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/prosperity', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'peace on the earth' is coherent in a proclamation of divine blessing.

טוב (consonants טוב): Candidates: H2895 'to be good (verb)', H2896 'good (adjective/noun)', H2897 'Tob (place)', H2898 'goodness/the best'. Chose H2896 as an adjective modifying 'favor'—'good favor/goodwill' toward people.
textual_notes: עלוי has no Strong's candidates provided. It could be a noun meaning 'exaltation/elevation' from the root עלה, or potentially an Aramaic-influenced form. It functions here as the subject: 'Exaltation [will be] to God most high.'
לאנשים has no Strong's candidates provided. Standard plural of איש (man/person) with preposition ל. It could also be parsed as אנשים from אנוש (mortal human).

The phrase מרצון טוב could be read as 'of good favor' (God's goodwill toward people) or 'of [people of] good will' (people who have good will). The Hebrew word order suggests 'favor good' as an attributive phrase modifying the kind of favor.

verses.literal: Exaltation will-be to-God most-high and-in-the-earth peace to-people of-favor good

verses.translation: And when the messengers [angels] departed from them, ascending and descending to the heavens [skies], the shepherds [were] speaking among themselves, saying: Let us cross over to Bethlehem [House of Bread] and see this thing [word, matter] which God [the Mighty One] is bringing about and has revealed to us
words: they departed / journeyed (qal perfect 3cp of נסע)
and descending (qal participle mp of ירד)
to the heavens (לשמים with ש missing/damaged)
the shepherds (qal participle mp of רעה)
let us cross over (qal cohortative 1cp of עבר)
in Beth / in the house of
and let us see (qal cohortative 1cp of ראה)
doing / making (qal participle ms of עשה)
and has shown / revealed (hiphil perfect 3fs of ראה)

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants ו+כ+אשר): Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר ('as/when') is a standard temporal conjunction that fits: 'and when the angels departed.'

ובירך: The candidates list H3409 'thigh' for ירך, but the form ובירך is clearly ו + בירך from ברך (to bless) in piel perfect 3ms. The consonants ב-ר-ך are the root here, not י-ר-ך. The candidate listing is misleading — the root is ברך not ירך. Reading: 'and he blessed.'
האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H410 because 'he blessed the God' is the natural object of blessing in a temple scene.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 same (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562 same, H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because 'and said' introduces the speech that follows.

verses.literal: And Shimon took him in his arms and blessed the God and said

verses.translation: Lord, now you [are] releasing [or: letting go] your servant according to your words [or: your promise] in peace [wholeness, well-being].

translation_notes: אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Shimon is addressing God as 'Lord/Sovereign.'
אתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'Lord, now you release' addresses God in second person.
בשלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/wholeness', H7966 'a requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'in peace' describes the manner of the servant's release.
textual_notes: עזוב — from root עזב (to leave, abandon, release). The form could be an imperative ('release!'), a participle ('releasing'), or an infinitive absolute. Context of address to God ('Lord, now you...') suggests either imperative or participle. The lack of explicit verb morphology markers makes this ambiguous.

verses.literal: Lord now you release your servant according to your words in peace

verses.translation: For my eyes have seen your salvation [or: your deliverance, your peace, your wholeness].

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 because 'for my eyes saw' provides the causal explanation for being released in peace.
textual_notes: שלומך — 'your peace/salvation/welfare': from שלום (H7965). In this context, referring to what Shimon's eyes have seen, this likely refers to the divine salvation/deliverance embodied in the child Yeshua. The word שלום encompasses peace, wholeness, welfare, and salvation — all may be in view here. This is notably not the word ישועה (salvation) but שלום, suggesting the emphasis is on wholeness/completeness of God's redemptive act.

verses.literal: For my eyes saw your salvation

verses.translation: that you have prepared [established, made ready] before the face [in the presence] of all the people

translation_notes: שהכינות: No Strong's candidates provided. Parsing as ש (relative particle 'that') + הכינות (Hiphil 2ms/2fs perfect of כון 'to establish/prepare'). The form means 'that you prepared/established.'
העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 (Aramaic 'with'). With the definite article ה, this is clearly 'the people' (H5971), not the preposition 'with.'

verses.literal: that you prepared before the face of all the people

verses.translation: that they will be as a light [illumination] and a declaration [revelation] to the peoples and a help [girding, strength] [for] Israel your people

translation_notes: שיהיו: No candidates provided. Parsing as ש (relative 'that') + יהיו (Qal imperfect 3mp of היה 'to be'): 'that they will be.'

באור: Candidates: H215 'to be luminous', H216 'illumination/luminary', H217 'flame/the East', H218 'Ur'. With prefix ב ('in/as'), H216 'illumination/light' fits naturally: 'as a light' or 'in light.' The context of revelation to peoples supports this.
והגדת: No candidates provided. Parsing as ו + הגדת, from root נגד (Hiphil noun form), meaning 'declaration/telling.' This is a nominal form meaning 'and a declaration.'
לעמים: No candidates provided separately but עם has H5971 'people.' With ל prefix and ים plural: 'to the peoples.'
ואזרת: No candidates provided. Parsing as ו + אזרת, from root עזר 'to help' or אזר 'to gird.' In context of strengthening Israel, both work. Choosing 'help/girding' as the meaning.
עמך: Parsing as עם + ך (2ms possessive suffix): 'your people.'
textual_notes: ואזרת could derive from אזר 'to gird/strengthen' or עזר 'to help.' Both produce coherent readings in context of Israel. The consonants favor אזר 'girding/strengthening.'

verses.literal: that they will be as a light and a declaration to the peoples and a help [to] Israel your people

verses.translation: And his father and his mother were astonished [amazed, marveling] at those things that were spoken concerning him

translation_notes: ואביו: ו + אב + יו: 'and his father.'
ואמו: ו + אם + ו: 'and his mother.'
תמהים: Plural participle from תמה 'to be amazed/astonished.' Meaning 'marveling/astonished.'
מאותן: מ (from) + אותן (those, feminine demonstrative pronoun in later Hebrew): 'from those.'
הדברים: ה + דברים, plural of דבר 'word/thing': 'the words/things.'
ש: Relative particle: 'that/which.'
נאמרו: Niphal perfect 3mp of אמר 'to say': 'were spoken.'
ממנו: מ + מנו 'from him/about him.'
והיה: Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Jah.' H1961 fits as the narrative verb 'and he was/it was.'
textual_notes: The words ירושלים, בירושלים, ירושלם appear to be scribal repetitions or marginal variants of 'Jerusalem/in Jerusalem' that were incorporated into the text. Similarly ושמו ('and his name') appears to be a fragmentary note or displaced text. These likely represent scribal glosses or textual corruption rather than continuous narrative.

verses.literal: And his father and his mother [were] marveling from those things that were spoken about him

verses.translation: And Shimon [Simeon] blessed them and said to his mother: Know that this one is appointed [laid, set] in Israel for a savior [deliverer] and for [the] redemption of many and for a sign [omen, portent] and against him [things] will be spoken

translation_notes: ושמעון: Candidates: H8095 'Shimon/Simeon', H4583 'abode', H4584 'Maon.' In a narrative where someone blesses and speaks, a personal name is required. H8095 Shimon fits.

בירך: The only candidate offered is H3409 'thigh.' However, the consonants ברך clearly correspond to the root ברך 'to bless' (H1288). The form בירך is a Piel perfect 3ms 'he blessed.' The H3409 candidate shares only ירך consonants. Choosing ברך 'blessed.'
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 (Aramaic), H561 'something said', H562, H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer.' With ו prefix and narrative context 'and said,' H559 is the clear choice.
שזה: ש + זה. Candidates for זה: H2088 'this/that' (demonstrative), H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that.' A sheep makes no sense; H2088 demonstrative pronoun fits: 'that this one.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 (Aramaic), H1933 'to be', H1934 (Aramaic). As pronoun in nominal clause: H1931 'he [is].'
מונח: The only candidate H5146 is נח 'Noah.' However מונח is clearly a Hophal participle of נוח 'to rest/lay/place' — meaning 'laid, placed, appointed.' The מו prefix is the Hophal participle marker.
ולאות: Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/omen.' Context of something set as a portent clearly points to H226 'sign.'
למושיע: Hiphil participle of ישע 'to save' with ל prefix: 'for a savior/deliverer.'
ולפדיון: ו + ל + פדיון from פדה 'to ransom/redeem': 'and for a redemption.'
textual_notes: נגדו at the end could be parsed as 'against him' (נגד + ו suffix) or as a verb from נגד 'to declare.' In context following נאמרו ('were spoken'), 'against him' as a prepositional phrase complements the verb: 'were spoken against him.' The ובו earlier may be a doublet or intensifier — 'and in/against him... were spoken against him.'

verses.literal: And Shimon blessed them and said to his mother know that this one he [is] laid in Israel for a savior and for a redemption of many and for a sign and against him were spoken

verses.translation: And a sword [knife, blade] will pierce [divide] and pass through her soul [being, life], so that [the] thoughts [intentions, designs] of many hearts will be revealed [made known, publicized]

translation_notes: ובסכין: ו + ב + סכין 'knife/blade.' No candidates provided. Standard Hebrew word for cutting instrument.
יחצו: From חצה 'to divide/pierce' — imperfect 3mp: 'they will divide/pierce.'
ויעברו: ו + יעברו, imperfect 3mp of עבר 'to pass through/cross over.'
נפשו: נפש + ו. The suffix could be masculine 'his' or (in later Hebrew convention) feminine 'her.' Given the context pointing to the mother addressed in the prior section, reading as 'her soul.'
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/in order that', H5669 'stored grain.' Context demands the conjunction: H5668.
לבבות: The candidate H956 (בות 'to lodge') doesn't account for the full word. לבבות is the plural of לבב 'heart' (H3824). Reading as 'hearts.'
מפורסמות: Later Hebrew form, Pual participle feminine plural of פרסם 'to publicize/make known.' No Strong's entry — this is a post-biblical Hebrew word meaning 'made known/revealed.'
textual_notes: נפשו — the suffix ו is typically masculine ('his soul'), but in this textual tradition it may serve for feminine ('her soul'), referring to the mother. Context from the preceding section (addressed to 'his mother') suggests 'her soul.'
ובסכין is unusual — traditional renderings of this passage-type use 'sword' (חרב). סכין specifically means 'knife.' This may be a translator's lexical choice.

verses.literal: And with a knife they will pierce and pass through her soul in order that [the] thoughts of many hearts will be made known

verses.translation: And [there was] a certain [one] daughter of Phanuel; she was from the tribe of Asher, and she was advanced [come] in days [years], and she had lived with her husband seven years from [the time of] her virginity

translation_notes: ובת: Candidates: H1323 'daughter', H1324 'bath measure', H1325 (Aramaic bath). Context of a named person's lineage: H1323 'daughter.'
אשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H836 'Asher (tribe)', H835 'happiness', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step.' Following מ<בט (tribe), this is the tribal name Asher: H836.
באה: Candidate H872 'an entrance.' However באה is also the Qal perfect 3fs of בוא 'to come/enter.' In the phrase באה בימים 'come in days' = 'advanced in age,' the verbal reading fits perfectly.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people', H5973 'with.' Before אישה 'her husband,' H5973 'with' is correct.
שבע: Candidates: H7646-7651. Before שנים 'years,' the numeral H7651 'seven' is the natural choice.
שנים: Candidate H8147 'two/twofold.' However שנים also represents the plural of שנה 'year.' Given it follows the number seven, 'years' is the correct reading.
ע ם: These appear to be the word עם 'with' split by a scribal break. Combined they read עם 'with' — connecting to בתוליה 'her virginity': 'from her virginity' or 'with her virginity.'
textual_notes: מ<מואל and מ<בט appear to contain damaged or unclear characters (marked with <). מ<מואל likely represents פנואל (Phanuel), and מ<בט likely represents משבט or שבט ('from the tribe of').
ע ם split across two tokens is likely a single word עם 'with.' The phrase עם בתוליה means 'from/since her virginity.'
שנים could be 'years' (plural of שנה) or 'two' (H8147). After 'seven,' 'years' is the clear reading.

verses.literal: And a daughter one of Phanuel she was from [the] tribe [of] Asher and she was come in days and she lived with her husband seven years with her virginity

verses.translation: And she was a widow for [up to] eighty-four years, and she never departed from the sanctuary [temple], performing service [worship] day and night with fasts and prayers

translation_notes: אלמנה: H490 'a widow/desolate place.' In context of a woman: 'widow.'
עד: Candidates: H5703 'perpetuity', H5704 'as far as/until', H5705 (Aramaic), H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'menstrual flux.' Before a number of years, H5704 'until/up to' fits.
ארבע: Candidates: H702 'four', H703 'four', H704 'Arba (a person).' Before ושלשים 'and thirty,' the numeral H702 'four' is correct. The phrase 'four and thirty' = thirty-four.
שנה: Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate', H8139 'sleep', H8140 'year (Aramaic)', H8141 'year', H8142 'sleep', H5089 'lamentation.' After a number, H8141 'year' is correct.
textual_notes: ארבע ושלשים שנה — literally 'four and thirty years.' This could mean thirty-four years as a widow, or the Hebrew translator may have been rendering 'eighty-four' (the age) with a textual confusion. The literal consonantal text says 'four and thirty.'

verses.literal: And she was a widow until four and thirty years and she [was] not moving from the sanctuary doing service day and night in fasts and prayers

verses.translation: And at that very moment [hour] she was giving thanks [confessing, praising] to YHWH, and she was speaking about him to all those who were waiting for [the] redemption of Israel — to Miriam [Mary] his mother — for redemption, and through him a sword [knife] will pass and pierce his soul, so that [the] thoughts [of many hearts] will be revealed. And you will draw near [and] you will trust.

translation_notes: שעה: Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look, a moment.' After באותה 'in that,' H8160 'moment/hour' fits as a noun: 'in that moment.'
מתודה: Based on H8426 תודה 'thanksgiving/confession.' מתודה is a Hitpael participle feminine of ידה: 'confessing/giving thanks.'
ליהוה: H3068 'YHWH' with ל prefix: 'to YHWH.'
מדברת: The candidate H1705 'Daberath (a place)' doesn't fit. מדברת is the Piel participle feminine of דבר 'to speak': 'speaking.'
לכל: H3605 'all' with ל prefix: 'to all.'
למרים: H4813 'Miriam.' With ל prefix: 'to Miriam.'
textual_notes: The sequence תהיו יהיו תהיו ת תהיינה יהיו appears to be extensive scribal repetition/corruption. Multiple variant forms of 'they will be' (feminine, masculine, 2nd person, 3rd person) are listed, suggesting a copyist was working through alternatives. Only one instance is needed for coherent text.

The passage from לפדיון ובו יעברו בסכין ויחצו נפשו שמחשבות appears to be a repetition or gloss from section 5 (Simeon's prophecy about the sword piercing the soul), incorporated into the Anna narrative. This may be a marginal comment that entered the main text.
ותקרבו תבטחו at the end appear to be displaced text or scribal additions — 'and you will draw near, you will trust' — not clearly connected to the preceding narrative.

verses.literal: And in that moment she was confessing/giving thanks to YHWH and she was speaking about him to all those who [were] waiting [for the] redemption [of] Israel to Miriam his mother for redemption and in him they will pass through with a knife and they will pierce his soul that thoughts will be will be will be will be will be and you will draw near you will trust

verses.translation: And when they had completed all the requirements [matters, words] of the law [statute, decree] of Moses, they returned to the Galilee [region, district], to the city of Nazareth

translation_notes: וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'step.' With כ prefix and ו conjunction, כאשר = 'when/as': H834.
דברי: Candidate H1704 'Dibri (a person).' However דברי is the construct plural of דבר 'word/matter' (H1697). Reading as 'matters/words of.'
דת: H1881 'a royal edict/statute' or H1882 (Aramaic). In the phrase 'matters of the law of Moses,' H1881 'law/statute' fits.
משה: Candidates: H4871 'to pull out', H4872 'Moses', H4873 (Aramaic Moses), H4874 'debt', H7716 'sheep.' After 'law of,' the personal name Moses (H4872) is clear.
בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city', H5893 'Ir (person)', H5894 'watcher/angel', H5895 'young ass.' Before נצרת (Nazareth, a place), H5892 'city' is correct.

verses.literal: And when they finished all [the] matters [of the] law [of] Moses they returned to Galilee to [the] city [of] Nazareth

verses.translation: And the child [boy, youth] Yeshua grew [became great] and grew strong, and [was] filled [with] wisdom, and the grace [favor, beauty] of YHWH was upon him

translation_notes: והנער: Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy/youth', H5289 'wanderer', H5290 'boyhood.' With definite article ה and followed by a proper name, H5288 'boy/youth' is correct.
ישוע: H3442 or H3443, both 'Yeshua.' H3442 chosen as the standard entry.

גדל: Candidates: H1431 'to be/make large/grow', H1432 'large', H1433 'magnitude', H1434 'thread/tassel', H1435 'Giddel (person).' In a sequence describing a child's development, H1431 'grew' (Qal perfect) is correct.
וחזק: Candidates: H2388 'to fasten/be strong', H2389 'strong', H2390 'powerful', H2391 'help', H2392 'power.' Parallel with 'grew,' H2388 verbal sense 'became strong' fits.

ומלא: Candidates: H4390 'to fill/be full', H4391 (Aramaic), H4392 'full', H4393 'fullness', H4394 'consecration', H3808 'not', H3809 (Aramaic 'not'). Before חכמה 'wisdom,' H4392 'full' or H4390 'was filled' both work. Choosing H4392 as adjective 'full [of].'
חכמה: H2451 'wisdom' vs H2452 'wisdom' (Aramaic). Hebrew context: H2451.
וחן: H2580 'grace/favor/beauty' vs H2581 'Chen (a name).' In the phrase 'grace of YHWH,' H2580 is correct.
יהוה: H3068 vs H3069. H3068 as the standard divine name.

verses.literal: And the boy Yeshua grew and [became] strong and full [of] wisdom and [the] grace [of] YHWH was with him

verses.translation: And his father and his mother would go [journey, travel] every year to Jerusalem on the honored [glorious, distinguished] day of Passover [the festival of passing-over]

translation_notes: שנה (consonants שנה): Candidates: H8138 'to fold/duplicate', H8139 'sleep', H8140 'year (Aramaic)', H8141 'year', H8142 'sleep'. Chose H8141 because 'every year' is the coherent temporal expression with בכל preceding it.
של (consonants של): Candidates: H7944 'a fault', H7945 'on account of/of'. Chose H7945 because it functions as a genitive particle connecting 'the honored day' to 'Passover'.

פסח (consonants פסח): Candidates: H6452 'to hop/skip over', H6453 'Passover (the festival)', H6454 'Paseach (name)', H6455 'lame'. Chose H6453 because the context is a pilgrimage festival in Jerusalem.

verses.literal: And his father and his mother [were] going in every year to Jerusalem on the honored day of Passover

verses.translation: And when the youth [boy, young man] Yeshua reached [attained] twelve years [of age], [they were] going up to Jerusalem according to their custom [practice, established way] on the day of the feast [festival, pilgrimage celebration]

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר is a temporal conjunction 'when' introducing the circumstantial clause.

הנער (consonants נער): Candidates: H5286 'to growl', H5287 'to tumble about', H5288 'a boy', H5289 'a wanderer', H5290 'boyhood'. Chose H5288 because the definite article + noun referring to a named person (Yeshua) fits 'the boy'.
שנה (consonants שנה): Chose H8141 'year' because it follows the numeral 'twelve' and denotes age.
textual_notes: עולים is a participle without explicit subject; context implies the family (his father and mother) were going up, continuing from section 1.

verses.literal: And when the boy Yeshua reached twelve years [they were] going up to Jerusalem according to their custom on the day of the feast

verses.translation: And when the days [of the feast] were completed, as they returned [turned back], the boy [youth] remained in Jerusalem, and his father and his mother did not notice [recognize, perceive] him [missing]

translation_notes: הנער (consonants נער): Chose H5288 'boy' as in section 2, referring to the same youth Yeshua.
ולא (consonants לא): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: כש<בין appears to have a damaged/corrupt consonant (<). Reading as כשבין or כששבין — likely כש + שבין (when they returned), from שוב (to return). The < may represent a damaged shin or other letter. The reading 'when they returned' fits the narrative context of departing Jerusalem after the festival.

הכירוהו — literally 'they recognized him' with negation: 'they did not recognize/notice [that he was missing]'. This could also mean 'they did not know [where he was]' — the verb נכר can mean to recognize or to notice.

verses.literal: And [were] completed the days when they returned the boy remained in Jerusalem and did not recognize [it] his father and his mother

verses.translation: And [they were] thinking [assuming, supposing] that he would be with the others who were going [traveling] with them, and so they traveled one day's [journey], and they searched for him among the rest [remainder] of the relatives [and] the acquaintances [known ones, familiar persons]

translation_notes: עם (consonants עם): Candidates: H5971 'a people/tribe', H5972 'a people (Aramaic)', H5973 'with (preposition)', H5974 'with (Aramaic)'. Chose H5973 because the preposition 'with' fits: 'he would be with the others'.
וכן (consonants כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'and so/thus' connects the assumption to the action of traveling.
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one day' is a standard temporal expression.
בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. Chose H996 because 'among the rest of the relatives' describes where they searched.

שאר (consonants שאר): Candidates: H7603 'leaven', H7604 'to remain', H7605 'a remainder', H7606 'a remainder (Aramaic)', H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Chose H7605 'remainder/rest' because 'the rest of the relatives' is the natural reading for searching among their wider circle. H7607 'kindred/flesh' would also work contextually but שאר + הקרובים reads better as 'the rest of the close ones'.
textual_notes: הנוכרים — could be read from נכר 'to recognize/be acquainted' (i.e., 'acquaintances, known ones') or from נכרי 'foreigner, stranger'. In context, searching among 'foreigners' after already searching among relatives makes less narrative sense. More likely this means 'acquaintances' — people known to them but not family. However, the consonants נכר more commonly yield 'foreign/strange' in biblical Hebrew. This text may use a later Hebrew sense where הנוכרים = 'the recognized/known ones'.
הלכו — the candidates list shows כו H3551 'window' but this is clearly the verb הלך (to go/walk) in 3rd person plural perfect, not a separate word. The system parsed the suffix incorrectly.

verses.literal: And thinking that he would be with the others who [were] going with them and so they went a day one and they searched for him among the rest of the relatives the acquaintances

verses.translation: And when they did not find him, they returned [went back] to Jerusalem to seek [search for] him

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Chose H834 'when' as temporal conjunction, same usage as section 2.
לא (consonants לא): Chose H3808 standard Hebrew negation particle.

verses.literal: And when not they found him they returned to Jerusalem to seek him

verses.translation: On the third day they found him in the Temple [sanctuary, holy place] sitting in their midst [among them], listening [paying attention, hearkening] to them and questioning [asking] them

translation_notes: במקדש (consonants מקדש): H4720 'a consecrated place, sanctuary, palace'. The context of Jerusalem pilgrimage and teachers makes 'the Temple/sanctuary' the clear reading.
textual_notes: ה<לישי — the < appears to be a damaged or uncertain consonant. Reading as השלישי (the third), which fits the narrative of finding him after a period of searching. The damaged letter is likely a shin (ש).
ושואלן — the suffix ן- (rather than ם-) for 'them' reflects a later/dialectal Hebrew form. This is a notable linguistic feature of the manuscript.

verses.literal: On the day the third they found him in the sanctuary sitting in their midst listening to them and asking them

verses.translation: And all who [were] hearing [listening to] him were astonished [amazed, marveling] at his wisdom [insight, discernment] and at his answers [responses]

translation_notes: וכל (consonants כל): Chose H3605 'the whole, all' as it introduces the collective subject 'all who were hearing him'.
textual_notes: ה<ומעין — the < again appears to be a damaged consonant. Reading as השומעין (the ones hearing), with the Aramaic/late Hebrew participial plural suffix ין-. The damaged letter is likely a shin (ש).
מתמיהין — hitpael or causative participial form with ין- suffix, from תמה (to be astonished). The ין- ending again reflects later Hebrew or Aramaic influence.

ומענהו — could be parsed as 'and his answer' (from ענה, to answer → מענה, an answer) or potentially 'and his response/testimony'. The singular construct 'his answer' fits the pairing with 'his wisdom'.

verses.literal: And all the hearers of him [were] astonished from his wisdom and from his answer

verses.translation: And when they saw him, the father and the mother were astonished [amazed], and they said to him: Why have you done this to us? For I and your father [have been] aching [grieving, in pain] and greatly [exceedingly, desperately] searched for you

translation_notes: האב (consonants אב): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'a green plant', H4 'a green plant (Aramaic)'. Chose H1 because the narrative context is parents finding their child.
והאם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H517 because paired with 'the father' — 'the father and the mother'.
למה (consonants מה): Candidates: H4100 'what/why/how', H4101 'what (Aramaic)'. Chose H4100 because ל + מה = 'for what' = 'why', a standard Hebrew interrogative.
כי (consonants כי): Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction introducing the reason for their distress.
אני (consonants אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the mother is speaking in first person.
ומאד (consonants מאד): H3966 'vehemently, greatly, exceedingly'. This is the only strong candidate; H108 'fog' does not fit.
textual_notes: כואבים — from כאב (to be in pain, to grieve). The candidates list shows H38 'Abijam' for אבים which is clearly wrong for this word. The full form כואבים is a participle meaning 'are aching/grieving/in pain'. This is the mother speaking of both parents' distress.
חפשנוך — 'we searched for you' with the archaic/emphatic 2ms suffix ך-. The verb חפש means to search thoroughly.

verses.literal: And when they saw him the father and the mother they were astonished and they said to him why did you do this to us for I and your father [are] paining and greatly we searched for you

verses.translation: And he said to them: What [is] this [that] you ask me? Did you not know that [it is] necessary [obligatory, required] that I be [occupied, involved] in those matters [things, affairs] that are of [from, belonging to] my Father?

translation_notes: והוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 as the independent pronoun 'he' introducing the speaker.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' fits the narrative of direct speech.
להם (consonants הם): The preposition ל + H1992 'them' = 'to them'.
מה (consonants מה): Chose H4100 as the interrogative 'what'.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun paired with מה = 'what is this'.
לא (consonants לא): Chose H3808 as the negation in a rhetorical question: 'did you not know?'
שאני (consonants אני): Chose H589 'I' with relative prefix ש = 'that I'.

שהן (consonants הן): Candidates: H2004 'they (feminine)', H2005 'lo!/behold', H2006 'lo/unless/whether'. Chose H2004 because 'that they are' (referring to הדברים) fits the clause 'the things that are of my father'.
מאבי: The candidates show H21 'Abi (a name)' for אבי, but this is clearly מ + אבי 'from/of my father', using the common noun אב (H1) with 1st person singular suffix.
textual_notes: שחוייב — this appears to be a passive participle from חיב (to be obligated/required), a form more common in Mishnaic/later Hebrew. It means 'it is obligated/necessary/required'.

באותן הדברים שהן מאבי — 'in those things/matters that are of my Father.' This could mean 'in the affairs of my Father' (i.e., in my Father's house/business/concerns). The phrase is ambiguous between 'in my Father's house' and 'about my Father's affairs/matters'. The Hebrew הדברים can mean both 'words/matters/things/affairs'.
מאבי — the מ prefix could be partitive ('from my father') or possessive ('of/belonging to my father'). In context, 'that belong to my Father' or 'that are of my Father' is the natural reading.

verses.literal: And he said to them what [is] this you ask me [do] not you know that [it is] obligated that I will be in those things that are of my father

verses.translation: And they did not understand [comprehend, grasp] the word [matter, thing] that he said [spoke] to them

translation_notes: והם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'and they' is the subject of the clause.

הדבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1907 'a vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'a pestilence', H1699 'a pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'the word/matter' that he spoke to them is the object of understanding.

שאמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 as the verb 'said' in the relative clause.
להם: Preposition ל + H1992 'them' = 'to them'.

verses.literal: And they not understood the word that he said to them

verses.translation: And he went down with them and they came to Nazareth, and he was submissive [or: obedient, subjected] to them. And his mother kept [or: preserved, guarded] all these matters [or: words, things] in her heart.

translation_notes: וירד (ירד): Candidates: H3381 'to descend', H3382 'Jered (proper name)'. The waw-consecutive prefix and the context of traveling to a destination clearly indicate the verb 'to descend/go down.' Chose H3381.

והיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah (sacred name)'. The waw-prefix with the surrounding narrative context of describing his ongoing state ('was subjected') clearly points to the verb 'to be.' Chose H1961.

להם (ל + הם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn in/rankle', H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. The preposition ל + pronoun הם giving 'to them' fits perfectly as the complement of 'subjected.' Chose H1992.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak/strong tree', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. None of these fit. In context, 'all ___ the words' demands a demonstrative pronoun 'these' (אלה as demonstrative, commonly listed under H428). The consonants אלה serve as the demonstrative 'these' in Hebrew, which is the only reading that produces coherent syntax here.
בלבה (לבה): Candidates: H3826 'the heart', H3827 'flame'. 'In her heart' is the natural reading for preserving words/matters internally. 'In her flame' would be bizarre. Chose H3826.
textual_notes: משועבד is a Mishnaic/late Hebrew passive participle from the root שעבד (to enslave, subject, obligate). It does not appear in the Strong's biblical lexicon. The form clearly means 'subjected/made subordinate/obedient.'
מקיימת is a late Hebrew participle from קיים (to uphold, preserve, fulfill). It also does not appear in the classical Strong's lexicon. The form means 'preserving/maintaining/keeping.'
אלה as demonstrative 'these' (H428) was not listed among the candidates but is the only consonantally and syntactically viable reading in 'all these the words.'

verses.literal: And he descended with them and they came to Natzrat and he was subjected to them and his mother [was] preserving all these the words in her heart

verses.translation: And Yeshua kept growing [or: increasing] in his wisdom and in years [or: stature, maturity] and in grace [or: favor, graciousness] before God and human beings.

translation_notes: מרבה: Candidates: H4766 'increasing/greatness', H4767 'abundance/great quantity', H7235 'to increase', H7236 'to increase (Aramaic)', H7237 'Rabbah (place)'. The participial form מרבה describing Yeshua's progressive growth fits H4766 'increasing' as an active participle/adjective. H4767 as a noun 'abundance' is possible but less natural as a predicate here. Chose H4766.

ובשנים (שנים): Candidate: H8147 'two/twofold'. However, the consonants שנים also correspond to שנים from שנה (H8141 'year'), meaning 'years.' In context of growing in wisdom and years and favor, 'years' (indicating age/maturity) is the coherent reading. H8147 'two/twofold' makes no sense here.

ובחן: Candidates: H974 'to test/investigate', H975 'watch-tower', H976 'trial', H2580 'graciousness/favor/beauty', H2581 'Chen (name)'. The preposition ב + חן: growing 'in favor/grace' alongside wisdom and years produces a coherent image of a maturing person gaining approval. 'In testing' or 'in a watch-tower' would be incongruous. Chose H2580.
textual_notes: ובשנים: The only Strong's candidate listed (H8147 'two/twofold') does not fit the context. The consonants שנים clearly correspond to the plural of שנה (H8141 'year'), meaning 'years,' which is the standard reading for growth over time. The candidate list appears incomplete.
The syntax of 'favor God and men' could be parsed as 'favor before God and men' or 'favor of God and of men' — the preposition governing the relationship is implicit.

verses.literal: And Yeshua [was] increasing in his wisdom and in years and in favor [of] God and men
